newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak SAX index dips 0.27 pts in listless trade.
newsitem.headline: Slovak SAX index dips 0.27 pts in listless trade.

text.p: Losses to the average price of shares of steel maker VSZ pulled the Bratislava Stock Exchange lower on Tuesday, as the bourse remains plagued with liquidity problems.

VSZ dominated the bourse's listed floor, closing unchanged at 650 crowns on a volume of 30,615 traded shares. But its average price, on which the SAX index is calculated, was 1.23 percent lower to drag index down 0.27 points to 185.82.
Brokers said the market continues to suffer from a lack of liquidity, with the range of the issues traded on the bourse needing to be widened.
"I think some new issues would help," Radovan Dzugas of Creditanstalt said. "It's a pity that our companies often prefer other ways to get funds, ignoring the capital market possibilities," he said.
Other Slovak blue chips were mostly quiet, or traded non-significant volumes of shares.
Oil refinery Slovnaft closed up 10 crowns at 800 crowns, while the largest country's commercial bank, VUB, gained 20 crowns to 1,700.
Overall volume decreased to 412,075 shares, from 1.27 million shares traded on Monday, while turnover eased to 188.84 million crowns, from 1.21 billion.
